No — leaf2 was not a real speedup, and pathtracer/ should not use it.

How I know:
1. The first leaf2 measurement looked great (33.5 ms vs ~46 ms), but that number was a bug: the leaf-2 traversal dropped the second triangle of every leaf. The image was visibly wrong and RMSE against the frozen default reference came out 0.79 versus 0.476 for the baseline, i.e. outside the 1.1x limit.
2. After fixing the dropped-triangle bug, leaf2 measured 49.8 ms against 49.7 ms for the round-2 tree in the same session — a wash, not a win.
3. The current 64-byte wide-node tree with ONE triangle per leaf measures 44.3–46.4 ms in the same sessions, so leaf2 loses to what is already in pathtracer/.

Why it loses: on this mesh (a thin closed shell) single-triangle leaves keep tight per-triangle bounds, so rays walk through far less empty space; merging two triangles inflates leaf bounds and adds back exactly the traversal work the smaller node count saved. Wide nodes already made leaves free (a leaf costs no node slot, just a payload word), so there was little left to gain from fewer leaves.

Current best in pathtracer/ is WIDE1 (2-wide 64-byte nodes, one triangle per leaf, interleaved TG4), verified at ~50.1 ms best / ~49.8 ms gpu best at 512x512/64spp. For completeness, the round-3 follow-on I just measured — 4-wide 128-byte nodes, which cuts tree depth 16 to 8 — also failed to win (44.2–47.2 vs 44.7–49.8 ms, tie-to-slight-loss), so it is not being adopted either.
